subject: Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan

messages.author: 1db85e2f569a5b5c
messages.subject: Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan
parts: I am wondering if anyone knows of published work where a Log Gaussian Cox process was fit using STAN. Thanks!

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan
parts:
No, but I'd also like to see an example. If nobody has one,
I'll probably write one myself over the next couple of months.
Our reading group here at Columbia is coming up to that chapter
in Kingman's book on Poisson processes :-)

I also just read this really neat paper by Miller, Bornn, Adams,
and Goldsberry on characterizing basketball shooters spatially:

http://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0942

It uses a Gaussian process for the means of
a log-Gaussian Cox process, with the added twist
of a non-negative matrix factorization to break the
basis of the Poisson process into a mixture.

- Bob

messages.author: 4200afc0918e2941
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan
parts:
Hi. I am very interested in getting this to work. The closest I'm aware of is probably the Kronecker GP stuff I've been working on--if you're happy with gridding up your counts, you can approximate an LGCP with a GP with Poisson observation model and use Kronecker (or FFT) for scalability [see my ICML paper, not Stan though]--but I did indeed run into issues with the non Gaussian observation model in Stan. Happy to share code in any case... And also this was before ADVI was around so that might help!

What's the scale of your data / observation window? Had you thought about how you'd like to set it up, e.g. using a grid as I did (following Diggle et al), or more like the sigmoidal idea [Adams 2009] or uniformization [Teh 2011]. I haven't thought yet about how we might implement those in Stan, but I'd be happy to discuss more.

Best,
Seth

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan
parts:
Thank you to everyone for the helpful comments!

Michael Betancourt, you mention that Euclidean HMC has a difficult time with LGCP. Is Riemann HMC better? and if so, is or will it be implemented in Stan?

Seth Flaxman, thank you for your paper reference! I have considered the grid approach as Diggle et al (2013) describes along with his r package LGCP. The only other alternative I had been aware of is INLA (Rue et al. 2009). My application window size is maybe moderate, a couple thousand grid cells.

--Beth

messages.author: f13fe7e880ed6103
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Log Gaussian Cox Process Model in Stan
parts:
Hi Beth. For a few thousand grid cells, I think that it'll eventually
get to the point that Stan can handle it, but it's not there yet.
It'll probably take Riemannian HMC (which should come at some point,
don't know the timeline) and some more work on dedicated matrix
algebra operations, e.g. some of the ones detailed here:
https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/60

I guess it depends on your timeline, i.e. if you need an answer
immediately, I'd try INLA (or GPstuff or GPy). But I certainly think
it'd be instructive to give it a go now in Stan, and try ADVI. Some
Stan code that might be helpful is at the end of my manuscript that's
in preparation, here's a link:
http://sethrf.com/files/fast-hierarchical-GPs.pdf

Seth
